newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Philphos plans fertiliser-for-debt swap.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Philphos plans fertiliser-for-debt swap.

text.p: Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corp (Philphos) plans to ask for a fertiliser-for-debt swap from its creditors, a senior Manila official said on Monday.

The Philippine and Nauru governments, which own Philphos, have agreed to pursue the plan to trim Philphos' foreign currency debts, Mariano Salazar, general manager of the Philippine government's National Development Co, told reporters.

Salazar said foreign debt would grow to the equivalent of 40 billion pesos at the end of 1997 from some 5.2 billion in the early 1980s. The company gave no details on the scale of the proposed debt swap.
Among the creditors of Philphos are Marubeni Corp, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd, Banco Exterior de Espana, and Societe Generale of Belgium.
The firm produces 1.17 million tonnes of compound fertiliser yearly, of which 70 percent is exported to Vietnam, Thailand, Burma and Indonesia.
